blocks.text: Managing clinical data in Excel on Mac

Clinical data managers rely on Excel when EDC systems do not offer enough flexibility. You likely spend your day cleaning data, checking for missing entries, and reconciling discrepancies between sites. Excel on Mac works well for these tasks if you know the right shortcuts and menu paths. Since you use a Mac, you might find that some Windows-based shortcuts conflict with system settings. Check your System Settings under Keyboard > Shortcuts if a key command fails.
How to speed up data reconciliation

Reconciliation requires comparing two datasets. You can use the [compare two columns in Excel](/how-to/compare-two-columns-in-excel) method to find differences quickly. If you have data that is formatted as text but should be numeric, use the [convert text to numbers in Excel](/how-to/convert-text-to-numbers-in-excel) guide to fix it. Keeping your data clean prevents errors in your final reports.
Using Lazur to find Excel features

When you are deep in a spreadsheet, you do not want to hunt for a specific setting. Ask Lazur where a button is. Lazur will draw a circle around it on your screen. This works for any menu, such as Data > Data Validation or Insert > PivotTable. You stay in the flow and get your work done faster.

blocks.text: Essential Excel tips for data managers

Data validation is your best friend. It prevents site staff from entering invalid data into your trackers. You can learn how to [use data validation in Excel](/how-to/use-data-validation-in-excel) to create dropdown menus. This limits entries to predefined options, which saves hours of cleaning later. Also, consider using [named ranges in Excel](/how-to/create-a-named-range-in-excel) to make your formulas easier to read and maintain.

Excel can handle up to 1,048,576 rows. However, performance may drop if you have too many complex formulas. Use [group and outline rows in Excel](/how-to/group-and-outline-rows-in-excel) to hide sections of your data that you do not need to see at the moment. This keeps your view clean and responsive. If your file is slow, check for circular references or unnecessary formatting.

Data privacy is essential in clinical trials. If you share a spreadsheet, ensure you [protect a sheet with a password in Excel](/how-to/protect-a-sheet-with-a-password-in-excel) to prevent accidental changes. This adds a layer of security to your work. Always verify that your file access permissions are set correctly before sending any documents.

You likely perform the same tasks every week. You can [record a macro in Excel](/how-to/record-a-macro-in-excel) to automate these steps. Once recorded, you can run the macro to perform the task in seconds. This is helpful for formatting reports or cleaning recurring data exports from your EDC system.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Excel files directly?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not edit files or click buttons for you. It points to where buttons are, guides you through steps, or answers your questions out loud.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Microsoft 365 for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, Lazur works in any app on your Mac, including Microsoft 365. It sees your screen and helps you navigate the interface.

faq.question: Is my clinical data safe when using Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur only sees your screen while you hold the shortcut. Audio and screenshots are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.
